name: I'm The Captain Now
aka: Look At Me, I'm The Captain Now
look: A still from Captain Phillips. Barkhad Abdi as the Somali pirate Muse stares wide-eyed and points two fingers toward his own eyes in a 'look at me' gesture, framed by the pillars and washed-out windows of a ship's bridge.
use: Someone or something seizes control of a situation it has no business running. The caption usually reads 'Look at me' on top and 'I'm the captain now' below, labeled with whatever just took over.
slots: bottom caption: who is in charge now, often 'I'm the captain now'
examples: The toddler holding the TV remote
describe: somali pirate gesturing for you to watch his eyes
captain phillips hijacker pointing two fingers at his eyes
skinny guy on a ship pointing at his own face
man with wide eyes announcing he is taking over
barkhad abdi pointing at his eyes on the boat
origin: From Captain Phillips (2013), where Barkhad Abdi's pirate Muse takes the ship and tells Tom Hanks's Captain Phillips, 'Look at me. I'm the captain now.'

variants.name: Captain Phillips - I'm The Captain Now
